newsitem.title: FINLAND: RISE IN FINNISH TAX REVENUE SLOWS MORE - FIN MIN.
newsitem.headline: RISE IN FINNISH TAX REVENUE SLOWS MORE - FIN MIN.

text.p: The rise in Finnish tax revenue slowed further in October, the finance ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.

The state's tax and tax related revenues rose 17.7 percent year-on-year in January-October, down from an increase of 18.3 percent in January-September and more than 10 percentage points off the 28 percent climb registered in the first half of 1996.

Overall, income tax collection rose to 100.87 billion markka in January-October, up 10.7 percent year-on-year. The pace of growth slowed from 11.3 percent in the first three quarters, and from a rise of 15.2 percent in January-June.
The state's January-October income tax revenue was 35.39 billion markka, up 26.9 percent.
State value-added tax revenue rose 18.6 percent to 36.19 billion markka while revenue from accise duties increased 6.2 percent to 19.36 billion markka.
The state's overall tax and tax-related revenues rose 17.7 percent to 102.03 billion markka.
The increase was partly due to the exceptionally low level of revenues in 1995, the finance ministry said, reiterating the reason stated throughout this year in its regular reports.
State expenditure excluding debt amortisation fell 1.7 percent year-on-year in January-October to 173.63 billion markka.
State debt servicing costs were 27.32 billion markka, up 18.3 percent year-on-year.

State transfers to municipalities fell 15.6 percent year-on-year in January-October to 28.20 billion markka, state transfers to households fell 5.7 percent to 34.56 billion markka, while state transfers to industry and business increased 9.4 percent to 14.40 billion markka.
The state's net borrowing requirement fell by 27.9 billion markka year-on-year in January-October to 29.5 billion markka, the finance ministry said.
